comment: The Crew: proto-CrossTalk work queue for cheap roster models. Read roots bound what crew members may look at; write roots bound where APPROVED output may land. Nothing outside these is reachable. deny_globs win over roots (secrets, git internals, app config).
fetch_comment: Domains crew members may fetch (e.g. "docs.godotengine.org"). Empty = web fetch disabled. Fetched pages are untrusted input: output stays staged and gated either way.

test_commands.comment: Commands the HARNESS may run for a test_triage task. A crew member can never choose or edit a command: it names one of these keys and the harness runs it. {python} is this interpreter. The code being run is the project's own, never agent-authored.

crew-tests.comment: The crew's own suite only (tests/test_crew.py): the rest of the repo has Unix-only tests that fail to collect on Windows.

script-tests.comment: For suites whose tests are standalone scripts (VtoT): runs each tests/test_*.py in its own process and prints a pytest-shaped summary.

lsp.comment: Language servers a job may use when its spec sets lsp: true (a campaign sets it with top-level "lsp": true). Members get symbols/definition/references/diagnostics as read-only tools, confined to their read roots; code jobs also get an 'lsp' gate rung that fails only on ERROR-severity diagnostics. Ported 2026-09-25 from Crush-lite's read-only LSP profile. Python: pylsp navigates (jedi) but has no linter plugin installed, so ruff's built-in server does diagnostics. pylsp cold-starts in ~23s on this machine, hence start_timeout_s.

bench_until.comment: Member -> local time the bench ends; ignored once it passes (crew/config.py benched_members). 2026-09-28 Kris: Gordon benched 24 h after his model (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on Synthetic) stopped answering: one request hung 14 min then 524, the retry never replied, a direct 60 s probe timed out while Hoss and Qwen answered in under 2 s.

rate_limit.comment: Published limits (https://synthetic.new/rate-limits, recorded 2026-09-21; details in crew/SYNTHETIC_LIMITS.md). Per pack: 500 requests/5h regenerating 5% every 15 min; $24/week credits regenerating 2% every 202 min; 1 concurrent request per model. Kris has 2 packs (1000 req/5h, $48/week, 2 per model) until 2026-09-30. Requests are weighted by the model's input price against Kimi-K3 = 1 (GLM-5.3-Flash ~0.1; measured 2026-09-20: a cheap-model call ~0.033). The provider's x-synthetic-quotas header is the truth and the governor reads it; the numbers here are the fallback before the first answer. credit_reserve_percent is kept for Kris and Crush.

defaults.budget_from_personnel_comment: 2026-09-25: a job's requests, tokens, working context and observation size come from crew/personnel.json and the member's own passing history (crew/personnel.py) instead of one number for everyone; the Inspector (crew/inspector.py) runs after every job. An explicit spec budget still wins. Set false to return to the flat defaults below.

max_tokens_by_member.comment: Output ceiling per member. Barry (GLM-4.7-Flash) and Nemotron reason at length before answering; at 16384 Barry returned three empty replies in a row, having spent 18-20k tokens thinking. A bigger ceiling costs tokens, which are cheap, and saves whole retries, which are not. 2026-09-20: Qwen hit the same wall on profiles.py - a ~200 line module cannot be re-emitted whole inside 16384, so three retries in a row died as budget_tokens without producing a file. Raised Qwen to 32768 and Hoss to 24576. 2026-09-21: Barry moved from GLM-4.7-Flash (archived; needed 49152) to GLM-5.3-Flash, and Gordon (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) joined; both start at 32768 until measured. 2026-09-21 (gl-std140): Barry on GLM-5.3-Flash spent 36,448 tokens reasoning against 32768 and was cut off before answering; raised to 65536, the provider's max_output_length for GLM-5.3-Flash. 2026-09-22: GLM-4.7-Flash reactivated as its own member, Larry (separate from Barry) - starts at its old measured ceiling, 49152, rather than re-measuring from 16384. 2026-10-07 (splat-camera-lock): Qwen was cut off (output_truncated) twice writing camera-limits tests (a long contract with a verbatim OrbitControls port to reproduce); raised Qwen to 65536. 2026-10-20 (photo_tools): Kimi set to 24576, the cap that worked with the 'think silently, read by a program' prompt on 2026-10-15 (PERSONNEL.md); at the 16384 default one reply spent it all thinking aloud.

claude_members.comment: Claude models on the crew, reached through the official Anthropic SDK (crew/claude_chat.py), billed by Anthropic rather than Synthetic. Added 2026-09-21 for Kris's experiment: plan in Opus 5, delegate every job to small agents, unify in Opus 5. Needs `pip install anthropic` and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY before a job can run.

deny_models_comment: Empty: nothing is refused. The list was a measuring tool (Kimi was denied on 2026-09-19 to read roster-only spend: $0.15 crew vs $1.00 Kimi in 24h). Division of labor now: Crush drives Kimi, Claude drives Claude, and both delegate bounded work to the Crew. The crew's DEFAULT member is still Hoss (defaults.assigned_to); a big model only runs a crew job if an architect names it in assigned_to, which would usually mean the task was mis-scoped.
deny_globs_comment: crew/hidden_tests is denied so a member can never read the tests that judge it, even if a task mistakenly widens its read roots. crew/campaigns is denied because a campaign file names every task and team.
read_roots_comment: 2026-09-21: Kris's AHK V1 Agentic Project added READ-ONLY so the crew can research how AutoHotkey v1 is used here. It is not a write root. Its .env files, .git, node_modules and .claude are refused by the deny globs above. 2026-09-22: octofriend-vanilla, Vocto, yetifriend and .octofriend added READ-ONLY - four dormant Octofriend-based experiments Kris wants archived (research -> cut list -> reorganize -> post-mortem -> zip; the folder-archaeology tool's next stage). None are write roots. .octofriend/config and .octofriend/data are NOT secret-named but hold app state (an engram.db, names.json) - excluded from anything the deterministic archive-apply step actually copies, regardless of what a member's cut list proposes; the usual deny globs (.env, secret/token/credential/pem/key, .git, node_modules) still apply to all four.
